newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower with restored gas.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower with restored gas.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open lower Monday as Gulf production returned to the market following last week's onslaught by Hurricane Danny, sources said.

August over-the-counter trade gradually softened ahead of the opening. At 0930, trade ranged from $2.13 to $2.14 after August settled slightly lower Friday at $2.168 per million British thermal units.
"There's a lot of production on its way back, and it's still cool in the Northeast," one trader said, noting slightly below-normal temperatures were also blanketing the southern plains.
Early cash prices were also feeling the brunt of restored production, as prices were talked at $2.16-2.19 at the Henry Hub.
Chart traders pegged August support at $2.138 and then at $2.12 and $2.051. Resistance was seen at the down trendline at $2.22-2.23, $2.29 and $2.36.
Columbia Gulf Transmission said it expects to fully restore service on its line later today, but about 150 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) was still missing from the market.
The gas processing plant in Venice, La., shut last week due to the storm, was providing about 50 mmcfd out of a possible total of 200 mmcfd to Columbia's system, a company spokesman said.
Transco also reported that service on its system was fully restored. The cuts had peaked at 350 mmcfd late Saturday.
In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped a couple of cents to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were off three cents to $2.09-2.14, while New York city gate gas lost about five cents to the mid-$2.50s.
